short: Large-vocabulary attempted-speech decoding in one participant holds; sensor, decoder and LM were already in the field, and the resolution attribution and cross-study ratios outrun the evidence.
position: The paper changed three components: intracortical arrays in area 6v (M05), a GRU phoneme decoder trained with CTC (M06) and an online 125,000-word language model (M07). Each was already in use before 2023 (ledger years, Appendix), so each is standard; a [later] system on the same design confirmed it at 2.5% WER. The main claim holds for one participant: 23.8% online WER at 62 words per minute on a large vocabulary was new for attempted speech, as a combination. The Abstract's credit to "these high-resolution recordings" is untested within the study, and the [concurrent] ECoG result is on a vocabulary about 120 times smaller (inference). The 2.7x and 3.4x margins are untested cross-study ratios, and the online numbers lack seeds and selection data.
